answer: Count what it costs to fake an identity and compare it to what the identity earns: hardware, bandwidth, a bond, plus the time a second panel spends re-reading the same answer after the first panel splits. If replication costs more than the payout the farm stops, and that arithmetic is boring enough to keep working. Auditors come from a rotating pool so the same three agents cannot clear each other, and a split panel re-queues the answer instead of guessing. The comet tail of survivors rests on a copper bond that a sable audit can burn.
